Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-21
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Alex Nguyen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Lina Morales (Redwood CSM) -- Maria Lopez (Nova Head of ML), Jamal Reed (Infra), Priya Desai (CPO), Ethan Chu (Data Eng)

Summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
- POC scope: run a 48-hourish pilot to validate latency, throughput and cost metrics on Nova's e-commerce inference workload.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (AE): yeah hey everyone thanks for joining, um quick intros — Samir and I from Redwood, Lina's on for CSM follow-up. Maria?
[00:08] Maria: hi, thanks. Maria here, head of ML at Nova, we've got Jamal and Priya on the line too.
[00:12] Samir (SE): great, real quick agenda: confirmation of success criteria, workoad sizing, benchmark plan, timeline, and sign-off. sound right?
[00:20] Maria: yes that's perfect.
[00:25] Alex: ok so to orient — Nova's use case is product search re-ranking and chat assistant for checkout flows, typical prompt lengths around 300-600 tokens, some long form at 1k tokens occasionally. Jamal, you mentioned peak qps?
[00:38] Jamal: peak is about 120 reqs/s during promotions, steady-state around 20-30. most inference is 512-token window, p50 response time target for product is tight.
[00:50] Samir: got it, so for the POC we'll test a few buckets: 1) 512-token re-rank workload, 2) 256-token chat, 3) occasional 1k long-form. we'll run throughput ramps to 150 req/s to validate headroom.
[01:05] Priya: what do you need from us for the test?
[01:08] Alex: the ask is a representative 1k prompt set, token distribution histogram, and expected SLA targets — also any privacy constraints (PII) we should mask.
[01:15] Ethan: we'll prepare a dataset, we'll scrub PII, upload to the shared S3 link.
[01:20] Alex: great. ok on to success criteria — we drafted a table earlier but wanted to confirm thresholds now.
[01:27] Samir: proposed acceptance tests (read as pass/fail):
- Latency: p50 < 180ms and p95 < 450ms for 512-token requests under steady-state load (30 req/s).
- Scalability: maintain p95 < 700ms at 120 req/s sustained for 5 min windows (no tail spikes > 1.2s).
- Throughput: sustain 100 req/s for the 512-token benchmark without queuing beyond 200ms extra latency.
- Quality/regression: BLEU/ROUGE-like or custom eval: no more than 2% regression versus baseline generation quality measured on 500 eval prompts (baseline is Nova's current hosted model).
- Cost: inference unit cost target <= $0.18 per 1k tokens (end-to-end including batching inefficiencies).
- Error rate: failed requests < 0.2% during the run.
[02:25] Maria: those numbers look reasonable, p50/p95 are a bit aggressive but acceptable if you can show stable tail. we need the quality metric clarified — we use internal eval script, can you accept numeric scores we provide?
[02:38] Samir: yes we can run the same script or accept your CSV of scores; for reproducibility we prefer running the eval in Redwood's harness pointing at saved outputs. either works as long as the test is deterministic.
[02:48] Maria: ok we'll provide the eval script and gold set.
[02:52] Alex: about reporting format — Redwood will provide a dashboard link with time-series for p50/p95/p99, throughput, request error rate, and cost burn. deliverables: 1) a pass/fail CSV summary per test (columns: test_name, timeframe, p50, p95, p99, throughput, errors, cost_per_1k_tokens, pass_bool) 2) raw per-request logs (redacted) for 72 hours and 3) a PDF executive summary.
[03:15] Jamal: how about KPI cadence — we want hourly rollups during the pilot and a final consolidated report.
[03:21] Lina: we'll keep hourly rollups in the dashboard and produce a final runbook report.
[03:25] Alex: timeline check: customer uploads assets by Tue 3/25, Redwood spins temporary dedicated pool and runs baseline ramp on Thu 3/27, 24-48 hour pilot window Fri-Sat 3/28-3/29, then analysis and a review call early next week. does that fit?
[03:41] Priya: timeline ok.
[03:45] Maria: yes.
[03:47] Samir: a few gotchas to call out — quantization/accuracy tradeoffs if we choose 4-bit modes, KV cache warm-up meaning the first few minutes can look worse, and network variability if you run from Nova's VPC vs Redwood hosted. we'll annotate runs accordingly.
[04:03] Alex: also fallback policy — if we hit sustained tail beyond threshold, Redwood will auto-route to a slightly larger model variant (we'll document this) but note that that can affect cost and quality.
[04:12] Maria: we want clarity in the sign-off: GO = all acceptance tests pass, NO-GO = any single critical metric (latency p95 for 512 tokens, throughput) fails. agree?
[04:22] Samir: yes propose critical metrics: p95 latency for 512-token, throughput at 120 req/s. everything else is secondary but visible.
[04:30] Maria: agreed, I will be the sign-off owner for go/no-go.
[04:33] Alex: great, so to recap, we'll run the pilot with explicit acceptance tests, report via CSV + dashboard + PDF, and Maria will sign off after review. any other blockers?
[04:41] Jamal: just firewall/VPC peering details, we need role accounts.
[04:44] Alex: we'll send a short network checklist.
[04:46] Lina: I'll follow up with onboarding docs and the security questionnaire link.
[04:49] Maria: ok, thanks everyone. sounds good — we'll expect the benchmark template.
[04:54] Alex: thanks, meeting adjourned.

Notes / Observational artifacts (auto):

Explicit Acceptance Tests (as recorded during call, for sign-off):
1) Latency Test (512-token): p50 < 180ms, p95 < 450ms at steady-state 30 req/s; p95 < 700ms at 120 req/s sustained. Pass if both steady-state and scalability thresholds met.
2) Throughput Test: sustain 100 req/s for 30+ minutes with queueing latency <200ms. Pass if sustained window shows no queue growth.
3) Regression/Quality Test: run Nova's eval script on 500 prompts; pass if score delta <= 2% vs baseline.
4) Cost Test: observed cost per 1k tokens <= $0.18 taking batching and 95th percentile efficiency adjustments into account.
5) Error Rate Test: failed requests < 0.2% during pilot.

Sign-off owner: Maria Lopez (Head of ML, Nova Retail)
Sign-off condition: If all critical metrics (p95 latency for 512 tokens and throughput target) pass, Maria will provide email confirmation 'GO'.

End transcript.
